ހައިސިއްޔަތަކުން ނޫން. ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ހައިސިއްޔަތުން މި މައިކު ކައިރީ ހުރެ މި ދަންނަވަނީ، ދީފައި އެހެރަ ގޯތިތައް، އަޅުގަނޑު އަދިވެސް ސަރުކާރުގައި ހަމަ އެދެމޭ އެ ގޯތިތަކުގެ ކޮށްފައި ހުރި މަސައްކަތެއް ކޮށްފައި ހުރިއްޔާ އޭގެ ބަދަލު ދީފައި، އެ ހުރިހާ ގޯއްޗެއް އަނބުރާ ދައުލަތަށް ނަގަން. އޭރަށް ދައުލަތަށް ވެސް، ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވެސް ގާތްގަނޑަކަށް ދިހަ ވަރަކަށް ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ، ދިހަ ވަރަކަށް ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ ރައީސް އެ ސަލާމަތްކުރެވެނީ. ވަރަށް ގިނަ ފައިސާ އެ ލިބެނީ. އަޅުގަނޑު މިއަދު ވަރަށް އުފާވާނެ، މި ގަރާރު ހުށަހެޅުއްވި މެންބަރު އެއީ އަޅުގަނޑާއި އަޅުގަނޑު މި ދެންނެވި މި ބިންތައް ދައުލަތަށް ނެގުމުގައި ވަރަށް އެއްގޮތް ޚިޔާލެއްގެ ބޭފުޅެއް. އެ ބޭފުޅާ ދެން ލިބޭ ފުރުޞަތުގައި އަޅުގަނޑުގެ މި ހުށަހެޅުމަށް ތާއީދުކޮށްދެއްވައިފިއްޔާ އަޅުގަނޑު ގަބޫލުކުރާނަން އެއީ މި ދިވެހި ފަސްގަނޑުދެކެ ލޯބިވާ މެންބަރެއްކަން. އިނގުރައިދޫ ދާއިރާގެ މެންބަރު މިއަދު އެ ހުށަހެޅުއްވި ހުށަހެޅުމަށް ކެންދޫ ދާއިރާއިން، ކެންދޫ ދާއިރާއިން މިއަދު ތާއީދު، ތާއީދު އައިސްފި ކަމަށް ވަންޏާމު އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަވާނަން ކެންދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރަކީ ވަރަށް އިޚުލާސްތެރި ދަރިއެއް ކަމަށް މި ދިވެހި ދައުލަތުގެ މައްޗަށް. މި ދިވެހި ޤައުމުގެ މައްޗަށް. ދެކޮޅުހަދައިފި ކަމަށް ވަންޏާމު މި ގަރާރު ހުށަހަޅާފައި މި އޮތީ ސިޔާސީ މަގުސަދެއް ހާސިލުކުރުމުގެ ބޭނުމުގައި. އެހެންވީމާ، ޙަޤީޤަތަކީ މިއަދު ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އެބަ ސާފުވާންޖެހޭ މި ސަރުކާރުން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއަށް، އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގެ 4000 ފްލެޓު ދީފައި އޮތް އެ ޙައްޤުވެރިންނަށް ޔަގީންކަން މި އަރުވަނީ، ސަތޭކައެއްނޫން، އެއްހާސް ޕަސެންޓު ޔަގީންކަން މި އަރުވަނީ އެއްވެސް އެ ދީފައި އޮތް ފަރާތަކަށް ނުޙައްޤަކުން ފުލެޓެއް ނާތުލާނެ. އަތުލާފައެއް ނުޙައްޤު ފަރާތަކަށް ފުލެޓެއް ނުދޭނެ. އަދި ޚާއްސަކޮށް އެ 4000 ފުލެޓަށް އެޕްލައިކޮށްފައި އޮތް ފަރާތަކަށް ނޫން ފަރާތަކަށް އެއަށް ވަނުމުގެ ފުރުޞަތެއް ވެސް ނުދޭނެ، އާ ފަރާތަކަށް. ނުދޭނެ. ނުދޭނެއޭ މި ދަންނަވަނީ. އެއީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް ސީދާ، އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ މެންބަރުންނަށް އަންގަވާފައި އޮތީ އެއްވެސް މެންބަރަކު މިއިން ކަމަކަށް ޚިޔާލު ވެސް ނުކުރައްޗޭ. މިއީ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީން ބަހާފައި އޮތް ގޮތަކަށް އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީން ދީފައި އޮތް ގޮތަކަށޭ މިކަން ދާނީ. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ރައީސަކީ ވަޢުދުވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ގޮތަށް ވަޢުދު ފުއްދަވާ ރައީސެއް އެއީ. މިއީ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ ކަހަލަ، ތެރެއިން ވެރިކަމަށް އަންނަ ކަހަލަ މިހެން ހެލޭފެލޭ ވެރިއެއް ނޫން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ މިހިރީ. މައިކު ވެސް މިހިރީ ހަލާކުކޮށްލާފައި. މި ވެސް ދޭތެރެއަކުން މި ކޮޅު ވެއްޓޭނެ ރައީސް އިނގޭތޯ. މިއަށް ވެސް އެބަ ޙައްލެއް ހޯދަންޖެހޭ. އެހެންވީމާ، ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، މި ވާހަކަތައް މި ދަނީ، މި ފްލެޓު ވާހަކަ ދެއްކިދާނެ ކިތަންމެ ދިގުކޮށް ވެސް. ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ދަންނަވައިލަން އޮތީ، ވެލިދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު އެ ފާހަގަކުރެއްވި ގޮތަށް އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އެ ދަނީ، ރާއްޖޭގައި އެހެރީ ހުރިހާ ރަށެއްގައި ފުލެޓު އެޅުމުގެ ކަންކަން އެ ދަނީ ކުރިއަށް. ބިންގާތައް އެ ދަނީ އެޅެމުން. އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް އެ ކަންކަން އެބަފެނޭ. ފުށިދިއްގަރުފަޅު އެ ދަނީ ހިއްކެމުން. އެތައް ހާސް ގޯޗެއް އެތައް ހާސް ފުލެޓެއް
އެތާ އެޅޭނެތަން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް އެބަ ފެނޭ. އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް ވެރިކަމަށް ނާދެވޭ ތަން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް އެބަ ފެނޭ. އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ ހަލާކުވަމުންދާ ތަން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް އެބަ ފެނޭ. އެ ބޭފުޅުންނަށް ހިތާމަ އެބަ ކުރެވޭ. އެއްގަލަކަށް އަރާ ވެރިއެއް އެތާކު ނެތް. އެހެންވީމާ، އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް ފާޑުފާޑު ގޮތްގޮތްވާނެ. ބައްލަވާ! މިތާ ވަޒީރުން ގެނެސްގެން ކޮން ސަކަރާތެއް މި ޖަހަނީ؟ މިއަދު ވެސް ހަމަ އިކޮނޮމިކް މިނިސްޓަރު މިތަނަށް ގެނެއްސިއްޔާ އެ ކުރާ ސުވާލު މާދަމާ ގެނެސް ވެސް އެ ކުރަނީ. އެހެން ސުވާލެއް ނުކުރޭ. ބަންކަރިންގ ޚިދުމަތް ކިހިނެއްތޯ؟ ޙައްޖު ކޯޕަރޭޝަނުން ޓޫރިޒަމުގެ މަސައްކަތް ފެށީމަ ވާނީ ކިހިނެއްތޯ؟ މި ދެ ސުވާލު މި އޮންނަނީ އަބަދު. މިއަދު ޖަވާބު ދިނަސް ހަމަ މާދަމާ ގެނެސްފައި ވެސް އަހާނެ ޙައްޖު ކޯޕަރޭޝަނުން ޓޫރިޒަމް މަސައްކަތް ފެށީމަ ކިހިނެއްތޯ ވާނީ؟ ޙައްޖު ކޯޕަރޭޝަނުން ވެސް އެ ކުރަނީ އެ ކުރަން އޮންނަ ގޮތަށް އެ ކަންކަން. މިސާލަކަށް ކެންދޫ ދާއިރާ މެންބަރު ލޯކަލް ޓޫރިޒަމް މަސައްކަތްކުރީމަ ކަމުދަންޏާ ކީއްވެތޯ ޙައްޖު ކޯޕަރޭޝަނަށް އެކަން ނުކުރެވެންވީ؟ ކުރެވެންވާނެ ނޫންތޯ؟ އަޅުގަނޑު އެކަން ކުރަންޏާ ޙައްޖު ކޯޕަރޭޝަނަށް ނުކުރެވި، ވެލިދޫ ދާއިރާ މެންބަރު ސަފާރީ ބޯޓެއް ދުއްވާތީ އެހެން މީހަކަށް ނުކުރެވެންވީ ކަމެއްތޯ؟ ހަމަ ޙައްޖު ކޯޕަރޭޝަނުން ވެސް ކުރެވޭނެ އެ އޮންނަ އުސޫލު ތެރެއިން ދެއްތޯ. އެހެންވީމާ، މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް މި ކަންކަން އެބަ އެނގޭ، ދަސްވާން އެބަޖެހޭ. ޙައްޖު ކޯޕަރޭޝަނުން މިފަދަ ވިޔަފާރިތައް ކުރީމަ ވެސް މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް އެބަ އެނގޭ ކުރިއަށް އޮތް މުސްތަގުބަލުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި ޙައްޖު ދަތުރުފަތުރުކުރާ މީހުންނަށް އެ ކަންކަމުގައި އަގު ހެޔޮކުރެވޭނެކަން. އެއީ އެ ތަންތާނގައި ފައިސާއިން އިންވެސްޓު އެ ކުރަނީ. އިންވެސްޓުކޮށްގެން އާމްދަނީ އިތުރަށް ލިބުނީމަ ދެން ޙައްޖަށް ދާ ބޭފުޅުންނަށް މިހާރު ފަސްދޮޅަސް ހާހަށް ދެވެންޏާ ދެން ދެވޭނީ ކުރިއަށް އޮތްތާ ސާޅީސް ހާހަށް. ދެން އަދި ޑޮލަރާ އެއްޗެހި އަގުހެޔޮވެ، މި ތަން ތަރައްޤީވާތަން ފެންނާތީ މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް އޮބިނޯވެގެން، ނުނިދިގެން މި ވާހަކަތަކާއި މި ގަރާރުތައް މި އަންނަނީ މި ތަނަށް. އަންނާނެ މި އެއްޗެހި. މިއީ އެމް.ޑީޕީއަށް މިވަރުގެ މެޖޯރިޓީއެއް އޮތް ނަމަ މި ގަރާރުތައް ހުށައެއް މިއަދަކު ނޭޅޭނެ. އެއީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް އެބަ އޮތް މި ގަވާއިދަށް ވަރަށް ކުޑަކުޑަ އިޞްލާޙެއް ހުށަހަޅައިލައިގެން، މިސާލަކަށް ބުނަންޏާ ކުއްލި މައްސަލަ ފުރަތަމަ މި އަންނަނީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް މިތާނގައި ބަލައިގަންނަން ފެނޭތޯ ނުފެނޭތޯ މި އަހަނީ. ކުއްލި މައްސަލައާއި ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި ގަރާރަކާ މާބޮޑު ތަފާތެއް ނެތް. ގަރާރަކަށް ނުޖެހޭ މިތާނގައި ބިލުގެ އުސޫލު އޮންނާކަށް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑު އަދިވެސް ތާއީދުކުރަނީ ކުއްލި މައްސަލައަކާ އެއްގޮތަށް މި ގަރާރުގެ މައްސަލަ ވެސް އޮންނަން. އެހެންނޫނިއްޔާ މި ތަނަށް ހަމަ މި ތާކުންތާކު ނުޖެހޭ މިކަހަލަ ބައިވަރު ގަރާރު ވަންނާނެ. މިއަދު ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި މި ގަރާރު ވެއްދުމުގެ ބޭނުމެއް ކަމަށް އަޅުގަނޑަށް ގަބޫލުކުރެވެނީ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގައި ރިޔާސީ އިންތިޚާބަށް ވާދަކުރާނެ ކަމަށް އިޢުލާނުކޮށްފައި އެބަ އޮތް ހަތަރު ބޭފުޅަކު. އޭގެ ތެރޭގައި ފެކްޝަންތަކެއް މިހިރީ. އެހެންވީމާ، މިއަދުގެ މި ގަރާރަކީ ވެސް ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި އިބްރާހީމް މުޙައްމަދު ޞާލިޙާ ދިމާއަށް އެއްޗެހި ކިޔުމަށް ޓަކައި މިތާ ކޮންމެވެސް ރޭވުމެއްގެ
ތެރެއިން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީން އައިސްފައި އޮތް އެއްޗެއް މިއީ. އެހެންނޫން ނަމަ ފުލެޓާ ބެހޭ ގަރާރެއް ނާންނާނެ މިތާކަށް ރައީސް. ފުލެޓާ ބެހޭ ގަރާރެއް މި މަޖިލީހަށް ހުށަހަޅާނީ އެ ތަނުން ފެކްޝަނަކުން އަނެއް ފެކްޝަނަށް ބެވުމުގެ ބޭނުމުގައި. ޝައްކެއް އޮތް ކަމެއް ނޫން މިއީ އިނގޭތޯ. އެހެންވީމާ، މިހާރު 11:40 ވެފައި، ވަމުންދާތީ އަޅުގަނޑަށް ވިއްސަކަށް މިނެޓު ވާހަކަދެއްކުނީ. އަޅުގަނޑަށް ދެއްވި ފުރުޞަތަށް ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް ޝުކުރުދަންނަވަމުން ވާހަކަކޮޅު ނިންމައިލާނީ. ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް ޝުކުރިއްޔާ.
speeches.en:
Thank you, Honourable Speaker. Yes! Now, you know, the debate we are holding in this chamber today began on a resolution submitted by an Honourable Member of the MDP, the Honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, Maaroof Zakir, expressing concern that under the Gedhoruveriyaa project many of the rightful recipients of the 4000 flats have not received them, or have been deceived, or have not been given them, and that it is being delayed, and seeking to find out how the members of this Majlis view the matter and what the members' views on it are. Yes! What I want to say about those 4000 flats they talk of is that it was the only work done by the outgoing government, done in the MDP's administration by taking about sixty billion rufiyaa, not sixty, perhaps a hundred and twenty billion rufiyaa, as debt for the state. When the administration ended, that work was not entirely complete. I estimate that about sixty or seventy percent of the work had been completed. Then, regarding those who got these flats, those to whom they gave flats, in their administration, in the MDP administration too, when the administration ended, there were cases submitted by the MDP to the ACC. That is, even the MDP noted that they had fought among themselves at the time in distributing those flats. For example, in the distribution in which the flats were divided up, a set number to the MDP Members of the People's Majlis of the time and members' families, a set number to ministers and ministers' families, and a set number to the heads of companies at the time and their families, because it was not divided equally, amid their fighting the case went as far as the ACC, during their administration. That was not something done by this administration. The member who submitted this will accept, you know, that it is exactly as he said, very well. So, it was the ACC that held up the handing over of the flats; at that time our Honourable President had not yet taken the oath. So, today the Maldivian people need to know about this in great detail. In reality today

I want to speak until 12 o'clock, Speaker, if the PNC has the time, you know. No, no, this is an issue the people need to know about in great detail. Then, before continuing, I must say this: under our Honourable President's tenure as housing minister, he at that time, with very hard work, with great capability and administrative skill, built 7000 flats. When the administration ended in 2018, those 7000 flats had documents handed to those who were to receive them, with about 99% of the work almost entirely completed and finished, you know, Speaker. The MDP came to power and the MDP... even today the Maldivian people still grieving over that are holding those documents, you know. However, the MDP must remember how the MDP acted that day. They cancelled everyone who held documents for those 7000 flats and gave them to people the MDP saw fit, something the MDP had no business dividing at all. The 7000 flats built by our President, today's President, at that time as housing minister, with very hard work, great sincerity and great capability: while a group held documents, documents given by the government of the time, the MDP came and took those things back, left them as they were, and divided up the 7000 flats among people the MDP wanted. So, that was in reality a very great crime committed by the MDP. The MDP is a party whose wickedness and tyranny the people know very well, you know. I will end that point there, you know. However, in our Honourable President's presidential pledges, he said at the time that, God willing, under his leadership he would build flats for those whose 7000 flats the MDP had taken back, and work to find a solution for them. He did not pledge to give those people even one flat from these so-called 4000 flats the MDP failed to finish. If it were the MDP, they would first cancel these 4000 flats entirely and, in reality, give flats from these 4000 flats to the people holding documents for the 7000 flats I mentioned, you know. The MDP must accept this justice very well. However, he does not act that way. Our Honourable President, in great detail, especially... in the People's Majlis, whenever there is a government, it is the Members of the People's Majlis who represent constituencies on the government's side. Whether it is flats in those constituencies, plots, land, loans

or medical treatment or anything at all, in most cases, in anything the people find difficult, the people call the member. So, in the matter of these flats too, in this Majlis there are a very large number of members, including 75 PNC members. We received very many phone calls. The guidance and advice our Honourable President has always given us is that he has decided to give the 4000 flats built by the MDP to the rightful recipients the MDP gave them to, in their own right, exactly as it stands for them. So the member who submitted this resolution today will know very well that not one flat of these 4000 flats has gone to the family of a member here, to the family of a government minister, or to any one of them. I say it boldly today before the Maldivian people: our family's full siblings and full siblings' children and others live in Malé. If it is proved that even one of them has received a flat from these, I will resign my seat and leave. That is how much certainty I give the MDP. The MDP will know, in submitting this, that if there is something bad in it, that bad thing is there because of the MDP. That it was the MDP that created that wrong. Look! At how the flats were given. In what way they set the criteria for this so as to give flats as they wished; that too must be considered. They set it so that, in checking a person's conditions, it was done through that island's island council, with the letter issued by that council as a condition. They considered that the most important document. This too is a very bad trap the MDP set, Honourable Speaker. Then what did they do? By paying money to some people in some island councils, they obtained letters for some people who have never lived in Malé. What kind of justice is this? This is how the MDP, MDP people, have done things. These are the crimes committed in the MDP administration. MDP people should be ashamed to submit resolutions, urgent matters and bills here, calling it a flat issue and this and that, to deceive the Maldivian people. I don't even think the MDP would dare to do such a thing. So, under this government, no rightful recipient of the 4000 flats built by the MDP will be left without a flat. Otherwise, within this, as I say, through a council to someone who has never lived in Malé; this too, it was the MDP administration itself that sent these things to the ACC and did this. Not us, this government. If a flat was given at the time to a citizen who has never lived in Malé,

the Maldivian people will decide whether getting it is just or unjust. Something due to people who lived in Malé for many years, 20 years, 30 years, given as a flat to a family that never came to Malé, on a letter issued by the council saying the person lived in Malé: if taking that back is unjust, then it is unjust. So the Maldivian people will decide whether it is just or unjust. So the MDP will know very well how this happened. Then, Honourable Speaker; look, something done up to now for the first time even in the world is giving plots from the seabed. And even giving them is not surprising. The greatest wonder is that registries were even made and handed over to people. These were taken from the open ocean, Honourable Speaker. Even in the world, people were astonished, are astonished at these things, even when neighbouring countries learned of this. Places like Dubai are people who reclaim from the sea, aren't they? Even they were astonished at it. In a country as economically poor and destitute as the Maldives, for the sake of power, out of greed, during the time they were campaigning in the election to come to power, it was not just one plot or two plots, Speaker. About forty thousand plots were registered and divided up for the purpose of getting votes. Two-thirds of those are at the bottom of the Giraavaru sea and the Fushidhiggaru sea, and another sea and the Maafushi sea, at the bottom of every sea. This is how these people have given plots and houses and flats to people. Isn't there not even a bit of shame in submitting things like this and talking about them here? So, in reality these people know that it is contrary even to the laws and regulations made in the Maldives; a plot registry for anyone should be made on land that has been reclaimed, after showing that land to the person. A registry cannot be made from the seabed and handed out. So that is not a way it can be given. Having given plots from the sea, a plot registry cannot be made. No law or regulation in the Maldives has been made that way. So these are people who have done things to that extent, Honourable Speaker. So these people might do anything of any kind, in any way, Honourable Speaker. So today I note with regret that the Gedhoruveriyaa scheme run by the MDP is in reality the biggest loss the state has suffered so far. The biggest loss given to the Maldivian people. Then look at a very expensive piece of land reclaimed with tax money received by the Maldivian state, Hulhumalé's Phase Two. Phase two. These people have it in the name of giving plots to Malé people living in Malé, Malé's... this too has been talked about in this Majlis for many days, Speaker. The reason this has to be said is that

this same one story keeps coming up repeatedly. There is no day without this flat story, this plot story. In reality this is not because these people don't know how these things happened. One Malé citizen is given a 1000 or 1200 square foot plot, sold by bidding for 10 million or 12 million rufiyaa. The next Malé person is given a 1200 square foot plot free, from the very same place in Hulhumalé. And the plots go to some MDP Member of the People's Majlis here at the time, or to someone in the member's family. Or to a minister of the time or someone from the minister's family. And then, as luck would have it, the plots received are in the same spot for child and father and mother, even when drawn by lot. Isn't this something neat too? A lot is drawn. Even when drawing lots, the plots fall for the minister and the minister's child, the minister's mother and father, in the same place, one next to the other in a single row. But you can also see the so-called housing ministry people standing right there putting papers into a jar like this and shaking it. So, that is the biggest magic trick ever performed in the Maldives. Isn't it, Maaroof? The biggest magic trick ever performed. So I want to say that too. The cost of the loss to the Maldivian state from those plots, approximately, as a loss, in the reviews by some committees here, comes to 13 billion rufiyaa. 13 thousand million rufiyaa, those plots. I... this is in no way something I say in the capacity of the majority, of majority leader here. I am revealing a feeling of mine today in the capacity of a Maldivian citizen. My view is that for the land that is still given out, given out free, if a perimeter wall has been built there, compensation for the wall should be given; if a plot has been built on, compensation for the plot should be given; and everything should be taken back to the state, you know. Even today, 99% of the Maldivian people will support this. That is, one person is given a flat on a paying basis. A big shot is given 1200 square feet of land free. What kind of justice is this? It means twelve million rufiyaa is being given for free. Another person is given it for three million rufiyaa on the basis of paying the money back over 20 years. So, what kind of thing are some of those given plots doing? Some of them have come to us to sell the plots. We are talking about plots given to live on. They have come to sell plots; plots worth 12 million rufiyaa are being brought to be sold for 8 lakh rufiyaa. Fine, since it is something got for free. Right? Good even if they get two lakh rufiyaa, since it is something got for free from the state. So, still, to the Maldivian government, in the capacity of a Maldivian citizen, in no way in the capacity of a PNC Member of the People's Majlis here. Not in the capacity of

majority leader. In the capacity of a Maldivian citizen, standing by this mic, I say: the plots that have been given out, I still request the government to compensate for any work done on those plots and take all those plots back to the state. Then the state and the Maldivian people will save about ten billion rufiyaa, about ten billion rufiyaa, Speaker. A great deal of money is gained. I would be very glad today; the member who submitted this resolution is someone who holds a view very similar to mine on taking the land I mentioned back to the state. If he supports this proposal of mine in his next opportunity, I will accept that he is a member who loves this Maldivian soil. If today support, support comes from Kendhoo constituency, from Kendhoo constituency, for the proposal made by the member for Inguraidhoo constituency, I will say that the Honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency is a very sincere son of this Maldivian state. Of this Maldivian nation. If he opposes it, this resolution has been submitted to achieve a political goal. So, the reality is that today the Maldivian people need to be clear that this government, our Honourable President, gives assurance to the rightful recipients to whom the MDP gave the 4000 flats, not a hundred, a thousand percent assurance, that no flat will be taken back unjustly from anyone it was given to. That no flat will be taken back and given to an undeserving party. And in particular, no party other than those who applied for those 4000 flats will even be given the chance to get into it, no new party. Will not be given. Will not, I say. That is what we, our members, have been told directly: that no member should even think about any of this. That this will go as the MDP divided it, as the MDP gave it. Our President is a president who fulfils his promises as he promises. Ours is not some flip-flopping leader of the MDP kind, who comes to power in between [unclear]. The mic here is broken too. This part will fall off at some point, Speaker, you know. A solution needs to be found for this too. So, in reality, Honourable Speaker, these stories go on; this flat talk can go on however long. What there is to say to the Maldivian people is that, as the Honourable Member for Velidhoo constituency noted, our Honourable President is moving forward with building flats on every island in the Maldives. Foundation stones are being laid. The MDP can see those things. Fushidhiggaru lagoon is being reclaimed. Many thousands of plots, many thousands of flats

the MDP can see will be built there. The MDP can see that the MDP cannot come to power. The MDP can see the MDP being destroyed. They are feeling regret. There is no leader there who stands on one rock. So the MDP will feel all sorts of strange things. Look! What agony are they inflicting by bringing ministers here? Even today, if the Economic Minister is brought here, the question they ask they will ask again if he is brought tomorrow. They ask no other question. How is the bunkering service? What happens when the Hajj Corporation starts tourism work? These two questions are always there. Even if answered today, if he is brought tomorrow they will still ask what happens when the Hajj Corporation starts tourism work. The Hajj Corporation too does those things in the way they are supposed to be done. For example, if it is fine for the Kendhoo constituency member to do local tourism work, why shouldn't the Hajj Corporation be able to do it? Shouldn't it be able to? If I do it, can the Hajj Corporation not? Because the Velidhoo constituency member runs a safari boat, is it something nobody else should be able to do? The Hajj Corporation too can do it, within the existing principles, right? So these people know these things; they need to learn. These people know that when the Hajj Corporation does such businesses, in the future it will be possible to make prices cheaper for people travelling for Hajj from the Maldives. That is, it invests money in those places. When income increases through investment, then those going on Hajj, if they can now go for sixty thousand, will be able to go for forty thousand in the future. And the dollar and things will get cheaper, and because they see this place developing, these people are uneasy and sleepless, and that is why these stories and these resolutions come here. These things will come. If the MDP had a majority of this size, these resolutions would never be submitted. That is, we have the option of proposing a very small amendment to these rules: for example, with an urgent matter, what comes first is asking whether we see fit to accept it here or not. In reality there is not much difference between an urgent matter and a resolution. A resolution here does not need to follow the procedure of a bill, Honourable Speaker. So I still support handling resolutions in the same way as urgent matters. Otherwise many resolutions like this, which do not belong here at all, will come into this place. In reality, I believe the purpose of bringing this resolution today is that there are four people in the MDP who have announced they will contest the presidential election. There are factions within that. So, today's resolution too is in reality something that has come from the MDP through some plan here to say things against Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.

Otherwise a resolution about flats would not come here, Speaker. A resolution about flats is submitted to this Majlis for one faction there to take aim at another. This is not something in doubt, you know. So, as it is now 11:40, I have spoken for about twenty minutes. I will end my remarks with many thanks for the opportunity given to me. Thank you very much.

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv: ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު. މިހާރު އަޅުގަނޑު ފުރުޞަތުއަރުވަން މި އޮތީ ހުޅުމާލެ އުތުރު ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު ޙުސައިން ޝަރީފަށް. މިހާރު މެންދުރު ނަމާދަށް ގޮވާ އެބަ 12:54 ގައި. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑު މިއަދުގެ ޖަލްސާ ކުރިއަށް ގެންދާނީ 12:45 އާ ހަމައަށް ކަމުގައި ދަންނަވަމުން ފުރުޞަތުއަރުވަން ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަން ހުޅުމާލެ އުތުރު ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު ޙުސައިން ޝަރީފަށް. މާފުކޮށްދެއްވާ! 11:54 ގައި ނަމާދު ވަގުތު ވާނީ. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑު ޖަލްސާ ކުރިއަށް ގެންދާނީ 11:45 އަށް.
speeches.en: Thank you, Honourable Member. I now give the floor to the Honourable Member for North Hulhumale', Hussain Shareef. The call to the midday prayer is at 12:54. Therefore, stating that I will continue today's sitting until 12:45, I give the floor to the Honourable Member for North Hulhumale', Hussain Shareef, to speak. Excuse me! The prayer time is at 11:54. Therefore, I will continue the sitting until 11:45.

speeches.name: Hussain Shareef
speeches.heading: ހުޅުމާލެ އުތުރު ދާއިރާގެ މެންބަރު ޙުސައިން ޝަރީފް ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އާދެ! ފްލެޓާއި ގޯއްޗާ ޚާއްސަކޮށް މާލޭ ސިޓީގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ ދިވެހި ލޮބުވެތި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ޙައްޤުގައި، ކަމެއް ހަދާފައި އޮތް ގޮތެއް ނޫނީ ހެދިފައި ހުރި ގޯސްތަކެއްގެ މައްޗަށް ވެސް ގަރާރެއް މި ތަނަށް ހުށަހަޅައިގެން ވާހަކަ ދައްކަން ފުރުޞަތު ލިބުނީމަ އަޅުގަނޑުގެ ހުރި ޖަޒުބާތާއި، ހުރި އިހުސާސްތަކާ އެއްކޮށް އަޅުގަނޑު މިއަދު ވާހަކަދައްކަން ބޭނުންވަނީ ހަމަ ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި ވެސް އަޅުގަނޑު އުފަން ބަހުރުވައިން. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ބައްލަވާ! މިތާ އަދެ ދޮހާ މާލޭ އުތުރުންގާއި ދެކުނުންގާއި އެތަންމިތަންނެން ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުނެ މި މާލެއަށް އާހު މި ވަޒަންވެރިވެންނަށް މި ދިމާކޮޅޫ ކޮން ކަމަކާތޯ؟ ބޯހިޔާވަހިކަމެކެ ބޭނުންވެގެން. އެކަމަކު ކޮންމެ ބައެކެނަސް ވެރިކަމަން އާހޮ މި ހަދަނަގޮތައްކޫ އެހެލާނަ އަމިއްލަ ބޮނޑިވަރާ ބޮނޑިކެރަންނަންވެގެން މި ކެރަނަ ކަމައްކޫ އެހެލާނަގެ ވެރިކަން ދިފާޢަކެރަންނަން ރައްޔިތެންނަގެ ޓެކްސް ފައިސާއިން ފައިސާ ނަގައިގެން އިމާރާތަކޮޓެފެއި ބޭނުން ބަޔަކަށް ދީގެން ބޭނުން، ބަޔަކަށް ކަންތެތި ބޭނުންވެނެ ގޮތަށް ކަންތެތި ކޮޓެފެއި ހުއްޓޫ. ދިވެހި ލޮބުވެތި ރައްޔިތުންނަ މިކަލެ ހިތާމަވެރިވެގެން ގޮހޮ، ނަފުސާނީވެގެން ގޮހޮ އެހެލާނަ ވާހަކާއްކޫ ދުނިޔެ ދީލެކޮޓެފެއި އޭނެވަރާވެގެން. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ކެހެނަކުންވެގެން މިކަމާ މި ވެންނޫ؟ މިވެނެ ގޮތާ އެނގެއި؟ ކޮންމެ ބައެކެންނާސް މިތާން އާހޮ މި ބޮނަންނޫ، ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވަޢުދު ފުއްދައިދެންނަންވެގެން މި މަސައްކަތާ ކެރަންނަ މި ބޮނަންނޫ ތޭމީހާނަ ބޭނުންވެންނައޫ ދިވެހި
ރައްޔިތުންނަގެ ޙައްޤު، ޙައްޤު ގޮތުގައި އަދާކޮށްދެންނަންގޭ. އެހެންކޭފޭ އެ ވާހަކަޔާ ދައްކައިފެއި ހަރާންބަޅުމަސް އެހެންނޫން މިކަމާ މި ކެރަންނޫ. ކެރަންތަނާ އަހަންނަށް ތިފެނެއި. އަހަންނަށް މި ފެނެންނައޫ ހަމަ ފުލެޓު ލިބެނެ މީހެންނަ ފުލެޓު ލިބެންނޫ. ގޯތި ލިބެނެ މީހުންނަށް ގޯތި ލިބެންނޫ. ދެނެ މީހުންނަށް ދެންނޫ. ކަނެ މީހުނަ ކަންނޫ، ބޮންނޫ. އެކަމަކު ޙައްޤުވެރިންނަށް ޙައްޤު ގޮތުގައި ދީފެ އޮން ތަނަކާ ނުފެނެއި. އެހެންވީމެއި މި އެރަންނޫ ރަނގަޅަކަށް ނުން މި ކަންތެތި. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ގާނޫނުން ބޮނަންނޫ މިހެންނުން މިކަމާ ކެރަންނަން. ގާނޫނުން ބޮނޮފެ އޮތަ ގޮތަށް މިކަމާ ކެރަނައެއްތަންނާ ޙައްޤުވެރިންނަށް ޙައްޤުގޮތުގައި ނުންތޯ ދެންނަން ޖެހެންނޫ. އެހެންނުން މިކަމާ ކޮޓަފެއި އޮއްތޫ. ދިވެހިރާއްދޭގެ ދެކުނަން ބަލައިލައި، ދެކުނުން ވަރަށް ގިނަ ބަޔެކެން މިތޯ މިތާ މާލެއަށް އާހޮ ބޯހިޔާވަހިކަމަން އެދީގެން. އެހެލާނަށް އެ ކަމާ ކޮށްދެންތަނަކާ ނުފެނެއި. 50 އަހަރަ ކަޑައްތުކޮށްލި. ދަފުތަރެކެ ކޭނެ އެއްތަކާ ލޭފެއިބައޮތެ. އޭނެން ބޯހިޔާވަހިކަމެން ނުލިބޮނެ. އަމިއްލަ ވަޒަނާ ދީލަކޮށްލިއާ. އަމިއްލަ އެޑްރެހާ ބަދަލަކޮށްލިއާ. އެހެނެއްކަމަކު އެހެލާނަށް ގޯއްތަކަ ނުލިބުނެ. ފުލެޓެކެ ނުލިބުނެ. އަހަންނަށް މި ފެނުނާ ދައުލަތުގައި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ޓެކްސް ފައިސާއިން ބޮޑެތި ލޯނާއި އެއްތެތި ނަގައިގެން ރައްޔިތުންގެ ބޯހިޔާވަހިކަން ގާއިމުކޮށްދެންނޭ ކޭގެން ކޮންމެ ރައީސަކުނަސް މި ވެންނޫ ހުސް ވަޢުދު. ހުސް ވަޢުދު. ތޯ ބަލައިލަ! މީނެ އެތެރަން އަތާ ލަންނަން ބޭނުންނުވެނެއެއްތެންނާ މިކަލެ އަދުގެ ޒަމާނީ ޓެކްނޮލޮޖީގައި އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، ވަރަށް ފަސޭހައިން ވަރަށް ޓްރާންސްޕޭރެންޓުކޮށް ވެންނަން އޮންނާ ކަންތެއްތާ ނޮކޮޓެ މި އޮއްތޯ ދީލަކޮޓެފެއި. އޮވެ ވޭލެއި އެކެ މީހަކު ބޮނަންނެއި ތަގެ ރޫމު ހުއްޓީ ބޮޑެ މިނާއި، ދިގެ މިނާއި، ވަޓަ މިނާއި، ފޮޑަލެ މިނާއި، އުސް މިނާއި، ތިރި މިނާއި މި ތެއްޔެހެއި ބައިބައި ފޫޓު އޮޑައިގެން ބަލައިގެން އަދި ވަފުދުވަފުދު ފޮނުވެއިގެން އެހެލާނަ ވޮންޑާ ގޮތާ ބަލައިގެން މި ތެއްޔެހެއި ކަމެއް ކޮށްލީވޭލެއި އާޚިރުގައި އެ މީހާއް ނުލެބެއި. ލެބެންނޫ، ލެބެންނޫ އެކެ ޢާއިލާއިން ލެބީފެއި ހުއްޓީ މީހާއަށް ހަމަ ލެބެންނޫ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އެހެންނު މި އޮއްތޫ ލެބީފެއި؟ އެކެ ޢާއިލާގެ ފަހަ މީހެންނަށް، ވެނެ މީހާން ގޯއްތައް، ވެނެ މީހާއް ފްލެޓާއް. އާނ! ހުތާއް ފުލެޓާއް. ދިޔާއް ފުލެޓާއް. ޅިޔަނާއް ފުލެޓާއް. އެކަމަކު ބޭނުންޖެހިފެއި ހުއްޓީ މީހާ 50 އަހަރު ވެފެއި ހުއްޓީވޭލެއި އެއްކިން ފުލެޓު ގަނޑަކަސް ނުލިބޮނެ. ޢަދުލުވެރިކަން ކޮބައިތޯ؟ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް ގޮންޑެ އިންނާވޭލެއި ބަލަންނަން ތި ޖެހެއި މި ގާނޫނުގެ ހަމަތަކުގެ މަންތެންތޯ މި ކަންތެތި ހިންގަންނައޫ. އެހެން ނޫން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް ހިނގަންނައޫ. އަސްލުއަސް، އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް އަސްލުއަސް ހަމަ ސީރިއަސްކޮށް ވިސްނަންޖެހެނެ ކަމެކެ މިއީ. ކޮންމެ ރައީސަކުނާ އާހޮ މި ވަޢުދު ވެންނޫ ތޭ މީހާ ވަޢުދާ ފުއްދަންނެންގޯއައު. ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީން ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ދީފެއި ހުއްޓީ މުދަލެއް ކެހެނަކުން ބޭނުން ގޮތަކަށް ތަބަކަކަށް ލައިފެއި ދިނެންނައޫ؟ ނުދިނެންނެއި. ގޯތި ވެސް ދީފައި ހުއްޓޫ އެހެން. ފުލެޓަސް ދީފެއި ހުއްޓޫ އެހެން. ރައްޔިތުމީހާގެ މުދަލާއި ފައިސާ ވާހަކާއްކޫ ވެރިއަކަށް އަންނާ މީހަކުން ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީއާ ޚިލާފަށް ދެންނެއި ގޮތެކެ
ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް އަހަންނަށް ކެއިދީހެލެ ނިކަން. ބަލަ ހަމަ ކޮންމެ މީހަކު ވެސް މި ބޮނަންނައޫ އެކެ މަގުން، އެކެ ފަރާތުން މި ދެންނޫ ނެވަ މިލިއަން، ދެހަ މިލިއަނަށް ގޯއްތާ ވިއްކަންނޫ. އެނެކެ ފަރާތުން ހިލެއި. ތޯ ބަލައި ކޮންފަދަ ބޮޑޮ ޖަރީމާއް މި އޮއްތޫ ހިނގުވައިފެއި. އޭނ؟ މިފަދަ ބޮޑޮ ޖަރީމާ ހިނގުވައިގެން ރައްޔިތުނަގެ މުދަލާއި ފައިސާ؛ ރައްޔިތުނަގެ ޓެކްސް ފައިސާއިން ތަންތަން ހިއްކައިގެން، ފުލެޓެ އޮޑައިގެން ކޮންމެ މީހަކުން އެ މީހެއްގެ، އެ މީހެއްގެ ވަޓައިގެން ވޮންނާ މީހުންނަން ތެއްޔެއިހެ އެއްތެކެ ބަހައި ނިންމެއިފެއި މިހެން ހެދީމެއި ކަމުނޯއެންނެން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. މިކަމާ ޖެހެއި އިސްލާޙުކެރަންނަން. ގާނޫނީގޮތުން، އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، ހަމަ އެއްކިން ވަގުތެ، ކުދެކުދެ ވަގުތެ ވިއްދެކެ އޮތަސް ހަމަ ދިނެފެހޭ ވަރަށް ރަނގަޅައެ. ވާހަކަ، މިއީ ވަރަށް ބޮޑަ މައްސަލައެކޭ. މި މައްސަލާއް ޤައުމީ ލެވެލެއްގައި ވިސްނައިގެން އެބަ ޖެހޭ އަހަނަ ވާހަކާއްކޫ މިކަން އަދޮ ދޮހާ ވިސްނުންތެރިކަމާ އެއްކޮށް ގާނޫނުން ކަށަވަރުކޮށްދީފައި އޮންނާ ކަންތެތި އަހަނަ އެބަޖެހެއި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ޙައްޤުގައި ކޮށްދެންނަން. ރައްޔިތުން ކޮންކަމަކާއިގެންތޯ އަހަނެ މިތާން ވަދޮވަފެއި މިތޯ؟ ޓެކްސް ފައިސާއިން އަހަންނަން ކަންނަންދީ ބަލަހައްޓައި، އިންޝުއަރެންސާއި ބޮޑެތި މުސާރައާ އެއްތެތި ދީފެއި އަހަނެ މިތާން ވަދޮވަފެއި އޮއްތޫ ރައްޔިތުންގެ ޙައްޤުގައި ވަކާލާތު ކޮޓެ، ޢަދުލުއިންސާފު ގާއިމުކޮށްދެންނަން. ރައްޔިތުން އެ ރައީސްމީހާ އިންތިޚާބު ކޮށްދީފެއި އޮއްތޫ ރައްޔިތުނައި، އަހަންނަސް އިންތިޚާބު ކޮށްދީފެއި އޮއްތޫ ރައްޔިތުނެއި، އަހަނެ ގާތު މި ބޮނަންނޫ އޭ ރައްޔިތުގެ މެންބަރު މީހާއޭ، އޭ ރައްޔިތުންގެ ޚާދިމު މީހާއޭ، އަހަންނަ މި ވޮންޑޫ ވަރަށް ހިތާމައާއި އަސަރު، އަހަންނަ ދީފެއި އޮތެ ފްލެޓުގަނޑާ ކަޓުވައިލިއާއޭ. ބޭނުން މީހަކަށް ދީފިއާއޭ. އެކެ ޢާއިލާގެ ދެވެނެ ތިނެވެންނަން ދީފިއާއޭ. ތޭމީހާނެ ވާހަކާއްކޫ މި އޮންނަ ހައުސިންގ މިނިސްޓްރީ ވުޒާރާއް ސިޓީ ލައިލިމާއޭ. ޖަވާބެކެ ނުދިނެއާއޭ. އެތައްކަލަކު ފޯނުން ގުޅައިލިމާއޭ، ޖަވާބަކަ ނުދިނޭ. މިނިސްޓަރު ވެސް ޖަވާބަކަ ނުދިނޭ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް...
speeches.en:
Thank you, Honourable Speaker. Yes! Having been given the opportunity to speak on a resolution submitted to this place about flats and land plots, especially about the rights of the beloved Maldivian citizens living in Malé City, about the way something has been done or the wrongs that have occurred, with the emotions and feelings I have, I truly want to speak today in my mother tongue. Honourable Speaker; look! Why is it that Maldivian citizens from the north and the south of Malé and from here and there come to this Malé and settle here? Because they need housing. But every group that comes to power, what they do is, in order to fill their own bellies and to defend their power, take money from the citizens' tax money, build buildings and give them to whoever they want, and do things the way certain people want. The beloved Maldivian citizens are today saddened and hurt; what they say is that they have given up on the world and are in despair [unclear]. Honourable Speaker; why is this happening? Do you know how this is being done? Every group comes here and says it is doing this work to fulfil its promises to the citizens, that what they want is to give the Maldivian

citizens their rights in the rightful way. Saying that, they do this for [unclear]. I see what is being done. What I see is that the people who get flats get flats. The people who get plots get plots. Those who give, give. Those who eat, eat and drink. But I do not see anywhere that the rightful owners have been given their rights in the rightful way. Therefore, these things are not being done properly. Honourable Speaker; the law says this must be done like this. Should it not be done the way the law says, giving the rightful owners their rights in the rightful way? That is not how this has been done. Look at the south of the Maldives; a great many people from the south have come here to Malé seeking housing. I do not see this being done for them. 50 years have passed. They have been put on some register. They have not received housing. They gave up their own home islands. They changed their own addresses. Yet they did not get plots. They did not get flats. What I have seen is that in the state, taking big loans and such from the Maldivian citizens' tax money, saying they will provide housing to the citizens, what every president does is make empty promises. Empty promises. Look at this! Because they do not want to hand it over [unclear], in today's age of modern technology, Honourable Speaker, things that could be done very easily and very transparently have not been done and have been left aside. Then a person is told his room is large on this side, long on that side, round, wide, high, low, all these measured in feet, and delegation after delegation is sent to look at how they live, and after doing all this, in the end that person does not get it. Does not get it, does not get it; the person who has already received one in a family gets it again, Honourable Speaker. Is that not how they have been given? To five people of one family: this person a plot, that person a flat. Yes! A flat for the son. A flat for the daughter. A flat for the son-in-law. But the person who needed it, who has turned 50, does not get even a single flat. Where is justice? Honourable Speaker; Honourable Speaker, sitting there, you must look at whether these things are being run within the bounds of this law. Honourable Speaker, they are not being run that way. Truly, Honourable Speaker, truly this is something that must be considered seriously. Every president comes and makes this promise, saying he will fulfil it. Has the Constitution allowed property given to Maldivian citizens to be put on a tray and handed out however one wishes? It has not. Plots too have been given like that. Flats too have been given like that. What I am saying is that one who comes to power gives away the citizens' property and money in a manner contrary to the Constitution

Honourable Speaker of the People's Majlis, please tell me. Look, everyone is saying that from one side they give, they sell plots for nine million, twenty million. From the other side they take [unclear]. Look at what kind of big crime has been committed. Eh? Committing such big crimes with the citizens' property and money; reclaiming places with the citizens' tax money, building flats, and each person dividing these things among those who circle around them and finishing it like this, is not acceptable, Honourable Speaker. This must be reformed. Legally, Honourable Speaker, even just one moment, a little time, twenty-something [unclear], it would be very good if it were given. The point is, this is a very big problem. This problem needs to be considered at a national level; what I am saying is that today, with wisdom, we must do for the citizens' rights the things that the law guarantees. Why have the citizens sent me here? Feeding me and looking after me with tax money, giving me insurance and large salaries and such, I have been sent here to advocate for the citizens' rights and to establish justice. The citizens elected that president, and the citizens elected me too; what they tell me is, 'Hey, people's member, hey, citizens' servant, what we feel is great sorrow and grief, the flat given to us has been cancelled. It has been given to whoever they want. It has been given to the second and third person of one family. When we write letters about this to the Housing Ministry, they give no answer. When we call by phone many times, they give no answer. The minister gives no answer either.' Honourable Speaker...

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
އަޅުގަނޑު ދެންނެވިން މިއަދު ސެޝަން ކުރިއަށް ގެންދާނީ 12:45 ކަމަށް. އަދި ވަގުތު އޮތިއްޔާ ދެން އަންނަ ބަހުސް އޮންނަ ވަގުތެއްގައި އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރަށް ފުރުޞަތު ލިބިވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެ ވާހަކަދަންނަވަމުން މިއަދު އަޅުގަނޑު ހަމަ ނިންމައިލާނީ އެއީ އަޅުގަނޑު ކުރިން ދެންނެވިހެން 11:54 ގައި މެންދު ނަމާދު ވަގުތު ޖެހޭތީއާ އެކީގައި އަޅުގަނޑު މިއަދުގެ ޖަލްސާ މިހާހިސާބުން ނިންމައިލާނަން.
# ނިންމުން
speeches.en:
I said that today the session would continue until 12:45. Stating that if there is time, the Honourable Member will get an opportunity at a time when the next debate is held, I will now conclude today, as I said earlier, because the midday prayer time falls at 11:54; I will end today's sitting at this point.

Closing

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ދެން މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖަލްސާއެއް އޮންނާނީ 29 އޮކްޓޫބަރު 2025ވާ ބުދަ ދުވަހު ހެނދުނު 9:00 ގައި.
والحمد للهّ رب العالمين މަޖިލިސް ނިމުނީ. ____________
speeches.en:
The next sitting of the Majlis will be held on Wednesday, 29 October 2025, at 9:00 in the morning.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Majlis has concluded. ____________
